"""Greedy template placement, one local day at a time.

For each local day of the week: while some (template, queue) pair still covers at least half an
hour of uncovered requirement, place the best-scoring pair on the available agent with the fewest
hours so far. Breaks go at the shift midpoint. Deterministic: fixed template order, agent ids as
the tie-break.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pandas as pd

from wfm import constraints
from wfm.ingest.loader import local_days
from wfm.roster import Agent
from wfm.scheduler.templates import Template, eligible, templates_for


@dataclass
class Shift:
    agent_id: str
    queue: str
    template: Template
    day: date
    segments: list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]
    intervals: list[datetime] = field(default_factory=list)   # grid slots the segments cover
    break_start: datetime | None = None
    break_minutes: int = 0

    @property
    def hours(self) -> float:
        return sum((e - s).total_seconds() for s, e in self.segments) / 3600.0


def _covered(segments, day_grid) -> list[datetime]:
    return [t for s, e in segments for t in day_grid if s <= t < e]


def schedule_week(req: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent], week: str) -> list[Shift]:
    tz = cfg["tz"]
    grain_h = cfg["interval_minutes"] / 60.0
    caps = cfg["weekly_hours"]
    max_run = cfg["max_consecutive_days"]
    templates = templates_for(cfg)
    queues = list(dict.fromkeys(req["queue"]))

    required = {q: dict(zip(g["interval_start_utc"], g["required"])) for q, g in req.groupby("queue")}
    cover = {q: defaultdict(int) for q in queues}
    cross = {q: defaultdict(int) for q in queues}    # agents on another queue holding this skill (min_cover)
    grid = sorted(set(req["interval_start_utc"]))
    z = ZoneInfo(tz)
    floors = {q: {t: constraints.floor(q, t, cfg) for t in grid} for q in queues}

    hours_used: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    days_worked: dict[str, list[date]] = defaultdict(list)
    shifts: list[Shift] = []

    for day in local_days(week, tz):
        day_grid = [t for t in grid if t.astimezone(z).date() == day]
        worked_today: set[str] = set()
        dead: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()   # (template, queue) pairs nobody can take today
        while True:
            best, best_val = None, 0.0
            for tpl in templates:
                segs = tpl.segments_utc(day, tz)
                ivs = _covered(segs, day_grid)
                for q in queues:
                    if (tpl.id, q) in dead:
                        continue
                    val = sum(min(1, constraints.uncovered(required[q][t], floors[q][t], cover[q][t], cross[q][t], cfg))
                              for t in ivs)
                    if val > best_val + 1e-9:
                        best, best_val = (tpl, q, segs, ivs), val
            if best is None or best_val * grain_h < 0.5:
                break
            tpl, q, segs, ivs = best
            cands = [a for a in agents
                     if q in a.skills and eligible(tpl, a.contract) and a.agent_id not in worked_today
                     and hours_used[a.agent_id] + tpl.hours <= caps[a.contract] + 1e-9
                     and not _would_exceed_run(days_worked[a.agent_id], day, max_run)]
            if not cands:
                dead.add((tpl.id, q))
                continue
            a = min(cands, key=lambda x: (hours_used[x.agent_id], x.agent_id))
            shifts.append(Shift(a.agent_id, q, tpl, day, segs, ivs))
            hours_used[a.agent_id] += tpl.hours
            days_worked[a.agent_id].append(day)
            worked_today.add(a.agent_id)
            for t in ivs:
                cover[q][t] += 1
                for other in a.skills & set(queues) - {q}:
                    cross[other][t] += 1

    place_breaks(shifts, cfg)
    return shifts


def _would_exceed_run(worked: list[date], day: date, max_run: int) -> bool:
    """True if working `day` would make more than max_run consecutive local days."""
    run = 0
    d = day - timedelta(days=1)
    while d in worked:
        run += 1
        d -= timedelta(days=1)
    return run >= max_run


def place_breaks(shifts: list[Shift], cfg: dict) -> None:
    """One break per long shift, on the covered interval nearest the shift midpoint."""
    rule = cfg["break"]
    length = timedelta(minutes=rule["minutes"])
    for sh in shifts:
        if sh.hours < rule["min_shift_hours"]:
            continue
        fits = [t for t in sh.intervals if any(s <= t and t + length <= e for s, e in sh.segments)]
        if not fits:
            continue
        mid = sh.segments[0][0] + timedelta(hours=sh.hours / 2)
        sh.break_start = min(fits, key=lambda t: (abs((t - mid).total_seconds()), t))
        sh.break_minutes = rule["minutes"]


def to_frame(shifts: list[Shift]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """schedule.csv rows: one per segment; the break sits on the segment that contains it."""
    rows = []
    for sh in shifts:
        for i, (s, e) in enumerate(sh.segments):
            has_break = sh.break_start is not None and s <= sh.break_start < e
            rows.append({
                "agent_id": sh.agent_id, "queue": sh.queue,
                "segment_start_utc": s.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
                "segment_end_utc": e.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
                "template_id": sh.template.id, "segment_idx": i,
                "break_start_utc": sh.break_start.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") if has_break else "",
                "break_minutes": sh.break_minutes if has_break else 0,
            })
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["agent_id", "queue", "segment_start_utc", "segment_end_utc",
                                     "template_id", "segment_idx", "break_start_utc", "break_minutes"])
    return df.sort_values(["segment_start_utc", "agent_id", "segment_idx"], kind="stable").reset_index(drop=True)
---TEMPLATES
"""Shift templates: local wall-clock segments on one local day; none crosses local midnight."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Template:
    id: str
    segments: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]  # (start_hour, end_hour) local, end may be 24
    eligibility: str = "all"               # "all" or a contract code

    @property
    def hours(self) -> float:
        return float(sum(e - s for s, e in self.segments))

    @property
    def is_split(self) -> bool:
        return len(self.segments) > 1

    def segments_utc(self, day: date, tz: str) -> list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]:
        """Local wall-clock segments on `day` -> UTC datetimes."""
        z = ZoneInfo(tz)
        midnight = datetime(day.year, day.month, day.day, tzinfo=z)
        return [((midnight + timedelta(hours=s)).astimezone(timezone.utc),
                 (midnight + timedelta(hours=e)).astimezone(timezone.utc)) for s, e in self.segments]


TEMPLATES: list[Template] = [
    Template("E8", ((6, 14),)),
    Template("D8", ((9, 17),)),
    Template("L8", ((13, 21),)),
    Template("N8", ((16, 24),)),
    Template("P6a", ((7, 13),)),
    Template("P6b", ((15, 21),)),
    Template("P4", ((10, 14),)),
    Template("S44", ((8, 12), (16, 20)), eligibility="all"),
]


def templates_for(cfg: dict) -> list[Template]:
    """Templates that fit inside the client's local operating hours."""
    open_h, close_h = cfg["operating_hours"]
    return [t for t in TEMPLATES if all(open_h <= s and e <= close_h for s, e in t.segments)]


def eligible(template: Template, contract: str) -> bool:
    return template.eligibility == "all" or template.eligibility == contract
---CONSTRAINTS
"""Minimum cover: queues that need a number of agents on shift whatever the volume.

A client config names them under `min_cover`, with the local hours the floor applies:

    min_cover:
      chat: {agents: 2, hours: [20, 24]}

The scheduler raises each interval's requirement on the queue to the floor; the evaluator reports
intervals below it as `min_cover` violations.

Cross-skilled cover (PR #31). An agent on shift on another queue who also holds the floor queue's
skill counts `cross_skill_weight` of an agent toward the floor (service default 0.5: a voice agent
with the chat skill picks up chats between calls). The weight applies to the floor only; required
agents from the staffing model are always counted on the queue itself.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo


def floor(queue: str, t: datetime, cfg: dict) -> int:
    """Agents the floor asks for on `queue` in the interval starting at `t` (0 if none applies)."""
    rule = (cfg.get("min_cover") or {}).get(queue)
    if not rule:
        return 0
    loc = t.astimezone(ZoneInfo(cfg["tz"]))
    h = loc.hour + loc.minute / 60
    lo, hi = rule.get("hours", cfg["operating_hours"])
    return int(rule["agents"]) if lo <= h < hi else 0


def weight(cfg: dict) -> float:
    return float(cfg.get("cross_skill_weight", 0.0))


def cover(on_queue: float, cross_skilled: float, cfg: dict) -> float:
    """Cover counted toward a floor: agents on the queue plus weighted cross-skilled agents elsewhere."""
    return on_queue + weight(cfg) * cross_skilled


def uncovered(required: int, floor_need: int, on_queue: float, cross_skilled: float, cfg: dict) -> float:
    """What the interval still lacks: the staffing requirement (agents on the queue) or the floor
    (cover as above), whichever is short by more."""
    return max(0.0, required - on_queue, floor_need - cover(on_queue, cross_skilled, cfg))
---ROSTER
"""Agents: data/agents/<client>.csv -> list of Agent."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pandas as pd

from wfm.config import DATA_DIR


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Agent:
    agent_id: str
    contract: str            # "FT" | "PT"
    skills: frozenset[str]   # queues the agent may serve


def load_agents(client: str) -> list[Agent]:
    df = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "agents" / f"{client}.csv", dtype=str)
    return [Agent(r.agent_id, r.contract, frozenset(r.skills.split(";"))) for r in df.itertuples(index=False)]

"""Shift templates: local wall-clock segments on one local day; none crosses local midnight."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Template:
    id: str
    segments: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]  # (start_hour, end_hour) local, end may be 24
    eligibility: str = "all"               # "all" or a contract code

    @property
    def hours(self) -> float:
        return float(sum(e - s for s, e in self.segments))

    @property
    def is_split(self) -> bool:
        return len(self.segments) > 1

    def segments_utc(self, day: date, tz: str) -> list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]:
        """Local wall-clock segments on `day` -> UTC datetimes."""
        z = ZoneInfo(tz)
        midnight = datetime(day.year, day.month, day.day, tzinfo=z)
        return [((midnight + timedelta(hours=s)).astimezone(timezone.utc),
                 (midnight + timedelta(hours=e)).astimezone(timezone.utc)) for s, e in self.segments]


TEMPLATES: list[Template] = [
    Template("E8", ((6, 14),)),
    Template("D8", ((9, 17),)),
    Template("L8", ((13, 21),)),
    Template("N8", ((16, 24),)),
    Template("P6a", ((7, 13),)),
    Template("P6b", ((15, 21),)),
    Template("P4", ((10, 14),)),
    Template("S44", ((8, 12), (16, 20)), eligibility="all"),
]


def templates_for(cfg: dict) -> list[Template]:
    """Templates that fit inside the client's local operating hours."""
    open_h, close_h = cfg["operating_hours"]
    return [t for t in TEMPLATES if all(open_h <= s and e <= close_h for s, e in t.segments)]


def eligible(template: Template, contract: str) -> bool:
    return template.eligibility == "all" or template.eligibility == contract
---CONSTRAINTS
"""Minimum cover: queues that need a number of agents on shift whatever the volume.

A client config names them under `min_cover`, with the local hours the floor applies:

    min_cover:
      chat: {agents: 2, hours: [20, 24]}

The scheduler raises each interval's requirement on the queue to the floor; the evaluator reports
intervals below it as `min_cover` violations.

Cross-skilled cover (PR #31). An agent on shift on another queue who also holds the floor queue's
skill counts `cross_skill_weight` of an agent toward the floor (service default 0.5: a voice agent
with the chat skill picks up chats between calls). The weight applies to the floor only; required
agents from the staffing model are always counted on the queue itself.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo


def floor(queue: str, t: datetime, cfg: dict) -> int:
    """Agents the floor asks for on `queue` in the interval starting at `t` (0 if none applies)."""
    rule = (cfg.get("min_cover") or {}).get(queue)
    if not rule:
        return 0
    loc = t.astimezone(ZoneInfo(cfg["tz"]))
    h = loc.hour + loc.minute / 60
    lo, hi = rule.get("hours", cfg["operating_hours"])
    return int(rule["agents"]) if lo <= h < hi else 0


def weight(cfg: dict) -> float:
    return float(cfg.get("cross_skill_weight", 0.0))


def cover(on_queue: float, cross_skilled: float, cfg: dict) -> float:
    """Cover counted toward a floor: agents on the queue plus weighted cross-skilled agents elsewhere."""
    return on_queue + weight(cfg) * cross_skilled


def uncovered(required: int, floor_need: int, on_queue: float, cross_skilled: float, cfg: dict) -> float:
    """What the interval still lacks: the staffing requirement (agents on the queue) or the floor
    (cover as above), whichever is short by more."""
    return max(0.0, required - on_queue, floor_need - cover(on_queue, cross_skilled, cfg))

"""Evaluate a schedule.csv against the required curve: attainment, hours, constraint audit.

A convenience for engineers. Contractual evaluation is performed independently against each
client's SOW.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pandas as pd

from wfm import constraints
from wfm.roster import Agent


def _parse(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = df.copy()
    for c in ("segment_start_utc", "segment_end_utc", "break_start_utc"):
        df[c] = pd.to_datetime(df[c], utc=True)
    df["break_minutes"] = df["break_minutes"].fillna(0).astype(int)
    return df


def coverage(sched: pd.DataFrame, grid, grain_min: int, skills: dict | None = None) -> tuple[dict, dict, dict]:
    """Per queue per interval: gross agents on queue, agents on break (overlapping the slot), and
    agents on shift on another queue who hold this queue's skill (`skills`: agent_id -> skills)."""
    gross = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    on_break = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    cross = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    step = timedelta(minutes=grain_min)
    skills = skills or {}
    for r in sched.itertuples(index=False):
        for t in grid:
            if r.segment_start_utc <= t < r.segment_end_utc:
                gross[r.queue][t] += 1
                for q in skills.get(r.agent_id, ()):
                    if q != r.queue:
                        cross[q][t] += 1
                if r.break_minutes and r.break_start_utc < t + step and t < r.break_start_utc + timedelta(minutes=int(r.break_minutes)):
                    on_break[r.queue][t] += 1
    return gross, on_break, cross


def evaluate(req: pd.DataFrame, sched: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent], week: str) -> dict:
    sched = _parse(sched)
    grain = cfg["interval_minutes"]
    grid = sorted(set(req["interval_start_utc"]))
    gross, on_break, cross = coverage(sched, grid, grain, {a.agent_id: a.skills for a in agents})
    h = grain / 60.0
    basis = cfg.get("attainment_basis", "service_level")

    sla, under, over = {}, 0.0, 0.0
    for q, g in req.groupby("queue"):
        met = tot = 0
        for r in g.itertuples(index=False):
            if r.volume <= 0:
                continue
            tot += 1
            scheduled = gross[q][r.interval_start_utc] - on_break[q][r.interval_start_utc]
            if basis == "coverage":   # PR #47: scheduled coverage of the requirement, capped at 1
                met += min(1.0, scheduled / r.required) if r.required else 1.0
            elif scheduled >= r.required:
                met += 1
            under += max(0, r.required - scheduled) * h
            over += max(0, scheduled - r.required) * h
        sla[q] = round(met / tot, 3) if tot else 1.0

    hours = float(((sched["segment_end_utc"] - sched["segment_start_utc"]).dt.total_seconds() / 3600).sum())
    return {
        "client": cfg["client"], "week": week, "intervals": len(grid),
        "sla": sla, "meets_target": all(v >= cfg["sla_target"] for v in sla.values()),
        "scheduled_hours": round(hours, 1),
        "understaffed_interval_hours": round(under, 1), "overstaffed_interval_hours": round(over, 1),
        "agents_scheduled": int(sched["agent_id"].nunique()),
        "violations": {**audit(sched, cfg, agents), "min_cover": floor_gaps(gross, cross, grid, cfg)},
    }


def floor_gaps(gross: dict, cross: dict, grid, cfg: dict) -> int:
    """Intervals where a `min_cover` queue has less cover than its floor (see wfm/constraints.py)."""
    return sum(1 for q in (cfg.get("min_cover") or {}) for t in grid
               if constraints.cover(gross[q][t], cross[q][t], cfg) < constraints.floor(q, t, cfg))


def audit(sched: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent]) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Count violations of the service's standard rules per agent."""
    by_id = {a.agent_id: a for a in agents}
    z = ZoneInfo(cfg["tz"])
    v = {"weekly_hours": 0, "consecutive_days": 0, "skill_match": 0, "no_overlap": 0}
    for aid, g in sched.groupby("agent_id"):
        a = by_id.get(aid)
        g = g.sort_values("segment_start_utc")
        hours = ((g["segment_end_utc"] - g["segment_start_utc"]).dt.total_seconds() / 3600).sum()
        if a is None or hours > cfg["weekly_hours"][a.contract] + 1e-9:
            v["weekly_hours"] += 1
        if a is not None and any(q not in a.skills for q in g["queue"]):
            v["skill_match"] += 1
        ends = g["segment_end_utc"].shift(1)
        if (g["segment_start_utc"] < ends).any():
            v["no_overlap"] += 1
        days = sorted({t.astimezone(z).date() for t in g["segment_start_utc"]})
        run = 1
        for d1, d2 in zip(days, days[1:]):
            run = run + 1 if (d2 - d1).days == 1 else 1
            if run > cfg["max_consecutive_days"]:
                v["consecutive_days"] += 1
                break
    return v
---WEEKS
"""ISO-week helpers for the reporting, export and notification commands.

Weeks are written `YYYY-Www` (ISO 8601, Monday first), the form `wfm run --week` takes. A client's
week runs from local Monday 00:00 to the next local Monday 00:00 in the client's timezone, so a week
that contains a DST change is 167 or 169 hours long and has a different number of intervals.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from wfm.ingest.loader import iso_week_monday

WEEK_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{4})-W(\d{2})$")
DAY_NAMES = ("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")


def weeks_in_year(year: int) -> int:
    """52 or 53: the ISO week of 28 December is always the year's last week."""
    return date(year, 12, 28).isocalendar().week


def parse(week: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """'2026-W44' -> (2026, 44). Raises ValueError for anything else, including W53 in a 52-week year."""
    m = WEEK_RE.match(week or "")
    if not m:
        raise ValueError(f"not an ISO week: {week!r} (expected YYYY-Www, e.g. 2026-W44)")
    year, wk = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    if not 1 <= wk <= weeks_in_year(year):
        raise ValueError(f"{week}: {year} has {weeks_in_year(year)} ISO weeks")
    return year, wk


def fmt(year: int, wk: int) -> str:
    return f"{year}-W{wk:02d}"


def monday(week: str) -> date:
    parse(week)
    return iso_week_monday(week)


def week_of(d: date) -> str:
    """The ISO week containing the date `d`."""
    iso = d.isocalendar()
    return fmt(iso.year, iso.week)


def add_weeks(week: str, n: int) -> str:
    return week_of(monday(week) + timedelta(weeks=n))


def key(week: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Sort key; plain string order is also correct for zero-padded weeks, this one validates."""
    return parse(week)


def week_range(first: str, last: str) -> list[str]:
    """Every ISO week from `first` to `last`, both included. Empty when last < first."""
    out, w = [], first
    while key(w) <= key(last):
        out.append(w)
        w = add_weeks(w, 1)
    return out


def days(week: str) -> list[date]:
    mon = monday(week)
    return [mon + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(7)]


def label(week: str) -> str:
    """'2026-W43' -> '2026-W43 (Mon 19 Oct - Sun 25 Oct 2026)'."""
    d = days(week)
    return f"{week} ({DAY_NAMES[0]} {d[0]:%d %b} - {DAY_NAMES[6]} {d[6]:%d %b %Y})"


def bounds_utc(week: str, tz: str) -> tuple[datetime, datetime]:
    """UTC instants of local Monday 00:00 and the following local Monday 00:00."""
    z = ZoneInfo(tz)
    mon = monday(week)
    start = datetime(mon.year, mon.month, mon.day, tzinfo=z)
    end = start + timedelta(days=7)   # wall-clock arithmetic: the next local midnight, DST included
    return start.astimezone(timezone.utc), end.astimezone(timezone.utc)


def week_hours(week: str, tz: str) -> float:
    start, end = bounds_utc(week, tz)
    return (end - start).total_seconds() / 3600


def expected_intervals(week: str, tz: str, grain_min: int) -> int:
    """Intervals of `grain_min` minutes in the client's local week (336 at 30 min without a DST change)."""
    return int(week_hours(week, tz) * 60 // grain_min)


def to_local(t: datetime, tz: str) -> datetime:
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        raise ValueError(f"naive timestamp {t!r}: expected UTC")
    return t.astimezone(ZoneInfo(tz))


def local_hour(t: datetime, tz: str) -> float:
    loc = to_local(t, tz)
    return loc.hour + loc.minute / 60


def in_operating_hours(t: datetime, tz: str, hours) -> bool:
    """True if the interval starting at UTC `t` starts inside the local operating hours [open, close)."""
    open_h, close_h = hours
    return open_h <= local_hour(t, tz) < close_h


def hour_starts(day: date, tz: str, hours=(0, 24)) -> list[tuple[int, datetime]]:
    """(local hour, UTC instant) for each whole local hour of `day` in [open, close). A local hour
    that does not exist (spring-forward) is skipped; a repeated one is listed once."""
    z = ZoneInfo(tz)
    out = []
    for h in range(int(hours[0]), int(hours[1])):
        loc = datetime(day.year, day.month, day.day, h, tzinfo=z)
        if loc.astimezone(timezone.utc).astimezone(z).hour == h:
            out.append((h, loc.astimezone(timezone.utc)))
    return out


def offset(t_local: datetime) -> str:
    """UTC offset of an aware datetime as '+HH:MM' / '-HH:MM'."""
    z = t_local.strftime("%z")
    return f"{z[:3]}:{z[3:]}"


def hhmm(t_local: datetime, day: date | None = None) -> str:
    """Local wall-clock 'HH:MM'. With `day`, a time at midnight after that day is written '24:00'."""
    if day is not None and t_local.date() > day and t_local.hour == 0 and t_local.minute == 0:
        return "24:00"
    return t_local.strftime("%H:%M")

"""Evaluate a schedule.csv against the required curve: attainment, hours, constraint audit.

A convenience for engineers. Contractual evaluation is performed independently against each
client's SOW.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pandas as pd

from wfm import constraints
from wfm.roster import Agent


def _parse(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = df.copy()
    for c in ("segment_start_utc", "segment_end_utc", "break_start_utc"):
        df[c] = pd.to_datetime(df[c], utc=True)
    df["break_minutes"] = df["break_minutes"].fillna(0).astype(int)
    return df


def coverage(sched: pd.DataFrame, grid, grain_min: int, skills: dict | None = None) -> tuple[dict, dict, dict]:
    """Per queue per interval: gross agents on queue, agents on break (overlapping the slot), and
    agents on shift on another queue who hold this queue's skill (`skills`: agent_id -> skills)."""
    gross = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    on_break = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    cross = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    step = timedelta(minutes=grain_min)
    skills = skills or {}
    for r in sched.itertuples(index=False):
        for t in grid:
            if r.segment_start_utc <= t < r.segment_end_utc:
                gross[r.queue][t] += 1
                for q in skills.get(r.agent_id, ()):
                    if q != r.queue:
                        cross[q][t] += 1
                if r.break_minutes and r.break_start_utc < t + step and t < r.break_start_utc + timedelta(minutes=int(r.break_minutes)):
                    on_break[r.queue][t] += 1
    return gross, on_break, cross


def evaluate(req: pd.DataFrame, sched: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent], week: str) -> dict:
    sched = _parse(sched)
    grain = cfg["interval_minutes"]
    grid = sorted(set(req["interval_start_utc"]))
    gross, on_break, cross = coverage(sched, grid, grain, {a.agent_id: a.skills for a in agents})
    h = grain / 60.0
    basis = cfg.get("attainment_basis", "service_level")

    sla, under, over = {}, 0.0, 0.0
    for q, g in req.groupby("queue"):
        met = tot = 0
        for r in g.itertuples(index=False):
            if r.volume <= 0:
                continue
            tot += 1
            scheduled = gross[q][r.interval_start_utc] - on_break[q][r.interval_start_utc]
            if basis == "coverage":   # PR #47: scheduled coverage of the requirement, capped at 1
                met += min(1.0, scheduled / r.required) if r.required else 1.0
            elif scheduled >= r.required:
                met += 1
            under += max(0, r.required - scheduled) * h
            over += max(0, scheduled - r.required) * h
        sla[q] = round(met / tot, 3) if tot else 1.0

    hours = float(((sched["segment_end_utc"] - sched["segment_start_utc"]).dt.total_seconds() / 3600).sum())
    return {
        "client": cfg["client"], "week": week, "intervals": len(grid),
        "sla": sla, "meets_target": all(v >= cfg["sla_target"] for v in sla.values()),
        "scheduled_hours": round(hours, 1),
        "understaffed_interval_hours": round(under, 1), "overstaffed_interval_hours": round(over, 1),
        "agents_scheduled": int(sched["agent_id"].nunique()),
        "violations": {**audit(sched, cfg, agents), "min_cover": floor_gaps(gross, cross, grid, cfg)},
    }


def floor_gaps(gross: dict, cross: dict, grid, cfg: dict) -> int:
    """Intervals where a `min_cover` queue has less cover than its floor (see wfm/constraints.py)."""
    return sum(1 for q in (cfg.get("min_cover") or {}) for t in grid

    """Count violations of the service's standard rules per agent."""
    by_id = {a.agent_id: a for a in agents}
    z = ZoneInfo(cfg["tz"])
    v = {"weekly_hours": 0, "consecutive_days": 0, "skill_match": 0, "no_overlap": 0}
    for aid, g in sched.groupby("agent_id"):
        a = by_id.get(aid)
        g = g.sort_values("segment_start_utc")
        hours = ((g["segment_end_utc"] - g["segment_start_utc"]).dt.total_seconds() / 3600).sum()
        if a is None or hours > cfg["weekly_hours"][a.contract] + 1e-9:
            v["weekly_hours"] += 1
        if a is not None and any(q not in a.skills for q in g["queue"]):

        ends = g["segment_end_utc"].shift(1)
        if (g["segment_start_utc"] < ends).any():

        days = sorted({t.astimezone(z).date() for t in g["segment_start_utc"]})
        run = 1

            if run > cfg["max_consecutive_days"]:

                break

def coverage(sched: pd.DataFrame, grid, grain_min: int, skills: dict | None = None) -> tuple[dict, dict, dict]:
    """Per queue per interval: gross agents on queue, agents on break (overlapping the slot), and
    agents on shift on another queue who hold this queue's skill (`skills`: agent_id -> skills)."""
    gross = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    on_break = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    cross = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    step = timedelta(minutes=grain_min)
    skills = skills or {}
    for r in sched.itertuples(index=False):
        for t in grid:
            if r.segment_start_utc <= t < r.segment_end_utc:
                gross[r.queue][t] += 1
                for q in skills.get(r.agent_id, ()):
                    if q != r.queue:
                        cross[q][t] += 1
                if r.break_minutes and r.break_start_utc < t + step and t < r.break_start_utc + timedelta(minutes=int(r.break_minutes)):
                    on_break[r.queue][t] += 1
    return gross, on_break, cross


def evaluate(req: pd.DataFrame, sched: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent], week: str) -> dict:
    sched = _parse(sched)
    grain = cfg["interval_minutes"]
    grid = sorted(set(req["interval_start_utc"]))
    gross, on_break, cross = coverage(sched, grid, grain, {a.agent_id: a.skills for a in agents})
    h = grain / 60.0
    basis = cfg.get("attainment_basis", "service_level")

    sla, under, over = {}, 0.0, 0.0
    for q, g in req.groupby("queue"):
        met = tot = 0
        for r in g.itertuples(index=False):
            if r.volume <= 0:
                continue
            tot += 1
            scheduled = gross[q][r.interval_start_utc] - on_break[q][r.interval_start_utc]
            if basis == "coverage":   # PR #47: scheduled coverage of the requirement, capped at 1
                met += min(1.0, scheduled / r.required) if r.required else 1.0
            elif scheduled >= r.required:
                met += 1
            under += max(0, r.required - scheduled) * h
            over += max(0, scheduled - r.required) * h
        sla[q] = round(met / tot, 3) if tot else 1.0

    hours = float(((sched["segment_end_utc"] - sched["segment_start_utc"]).dt.total_seconds() / 3600).sum())
    return {
        "client": cfg["client"], "week": week, "intervals": len(grid),
        "sla": sla, "meets_target": all(v >= cfg["sla_target"] for v in sla.values()),
        "scheduled_hours": round(hours, 1),
        "understaffed_interval_hours": round(under, 1), "overstaffed_interval_hours": round(over, 1),
        "agents_scheduled": int(sched["agent_id"].nunique()),
        "violations": {**audit(sched, cfg, agents), "min_cover": floor_gaps(gross, cross, grid, cfg)},
    }


def floor_gaps(gross: dict, cross: dict, grid, cfg: dict) -> int:
    """Intervals where a `min_cover` queue has less cover than its floor (see wfm/constraints.py)."""
    return sum(1 for q in (cfg.get("min_cover") or {}) for t in grid
               if constraints.cover(gross[q][t], cross[q][t], cfg) < constraints.floor(q, t, cfg))


def audit(sched: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent]) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Count violations of the service's standard rules per agent."""
    by_id = {a.agent_id: a for a in agents}
    z = ZoneInfo(cfg["tz"])
    v = {"weekly_hours": 0, "consecutive_days": 0, "skill_match": 0, "no_overlap": 0}
    for aid, g in sched.groupby("agent_id"):
        a = by_id.get(aid)
        g = g.sort_values("segment_start_utc")
        hours = ((g["segment_end_utc"] - g["segment_start_utc"]).dt.total_seconds() / 3600).sum()
        if a is None or hours > cfg["weekly_hours"][a.contract] + 1e-9:
            v["weekly_hours"] += 1
        if a is not None and any(q not in a.skills for q in g["queue"]):
            v["skill_match"] += 1
        ends = g["segment_end_utc"].shift(1)
        if (g["segment_start_utc"] < ends).any():
            v["no_overlap"] += 1
        days = sorted({t.astimezone(z).date() for t in g["segment_start_utc"]})
        run = 1
        for d1, d2 in zip(days, days[1:]):
            run = run + 1 if (d2 - d1).days == 1 else 1
            if run > cfg["max_consecutive_days"]:
                v["consecutive_days"] += 1
                break
    return v
---WEEKS
"""ISO-week helpers for the reporting, export and notification commands.

Weeks are written `YYYY-Www` (ISO 8601, Monday first), the form `wfm run --week` takes. A client's
week runs from local Monday 00:00 to the next local Monday 00:00 in the client's timezone, so a week
that contains a DST change is 167 or 169 hours long and has a different number of intervals.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from wfm.ingest.loader import iso_week_monday

WEEK_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{4})-W(\d{2})$")
DAY_NAMES = ("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")


def weeks_in_year(year: int) -> int:
    """52 or 53: the ISO week of 28 December is always the year's last week."""
    return date(year, 12, 28).isocalendar().week


def parse(week: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """'2026-W44' -> (2026, 44). Raises ValueError for anything else, including W53 in a 52-week year."""
    m = WEEK_RE.match(week or "")
    if not m:
        raise ValueError(f"not an ISO week: {week!r} (expected YYYY-Www, e.g. 2026-W44)")
    year, wk = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    if not 1 <= wk <= weeks_in_year(year):
        raise ValueError(f"{week}: {year} has {weeks_in_year(year)} ISO weeks")
    return year, wk


def fmt(year: int, wk: int) -> str:
    return f"{year}-W{wk:02d}"


def monday(week: str) -> date:
    parse(week)
    return iso_week_monday(week)


def week_of(d: date) -> str:
    """The ISO week containing the date `d`."""
    iso = d.isocalendar()
    return fmt(iso.year, iso.week)


def add_weeks(week: str, n: int) -> str:
    return week_of(monday(week) + timedelta(weeks=n))


def key(week: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Sort key; plain string order is also correct for zero-padded weeks, this one validates."""
    return parse(week)


def week_range(first: str, last: str) -> list[str]:
    """Every ISO week from `first` to `last`, both included. Empty when last < first."""
    out, w = [], first
    while key(w) <= key(last):
        out.append(w)
        w = add_weeks(w, 1)
    return out


def days(week: str) -> list[date]:
    mon = monday(week)
    return [mon + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(7)]


def label(week: str) -> str:
    """'2026-W43' -> '2026-W43 (Mon 19 Oct - Sun 25 Oct 2026)'."""
    d = days(week)
    return f"{week} ({DAY_NAMES[0]} {d[0]:%d %b} - {DAY_NAMES[6]} {d[6]:%d %b %Y})"


def bounds_utc(week: str, tz: str) -> tuple[datetime, datetime]:
    """UTC instants of local Monday 00:00 and the following local Monday 00:00."""
    z = ZoneInfo(tz)
    mon = monday(week)
    start = datetime(mon.year, mon.month, mon.day, tzinfo=z)
    end = start + timedelta(days=7)   # wall-clock arithmetic: the next local midnight, DST included
    return start.astimezone(timezone.utc), end.astimezone(timezone.utc)


def week_hours(week: str, tz: str) -> float:
    start, end = bounds_utc(week, tz)
    return (end - start).total_seconds() / 3600


def expected_intervals(week: str, tz: str, grain_min: int) -> int:
    """Intervals of `grain_min` minutes in the client's local week (336 at 30 min without a DST change)."""
    return int(week_hours(week, tz) * 60 // grain_min)


def to_local(t: datetime, tz: str) -> datetime:
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        raise ValueError(f"naive timestamp {t!r}: expected UTC")
    return t.astimezone(ZoneInfo(tz))


def local_hour(t: datetime, tz: str) -> float:
    loc = to_local(t, tz)
    return loc.hour + loc.minute / 60


def in_operating_hours(t: datetime, tz: str, hours) -> bool:
    """True if the interval starting at UTC `t` starts inside the local operating hours [open, close)."""
    open_h, close_h = hours
    return open_h <= local_hour(t, tz) < close_h


def hour_starts(day: date, tz: str, hours=(0, 24)) -> list[tuple[int, datetime]]:
    """(local hour, UTC instant) for each whole local hour of `day` in [open, close). A local hour
    that does not exist (spring-forward) is skipped; a repeated one is listed once."""
    z = ZoneInfo(tz)
    out = []
    for h in range(int(hours[0]), int(hours[1])):
        loc = datetime(day.year, day.month, day.day, h, tzinfo=z)
        if loc.astimezone(timezone.utc).astimezone(z).hour == h:
            out.append((h, loc.astimezone(timezone.utc)))
    return out


def offset(t_local: datetime) -> str:
    """UTC offset of an aware datetime as '+HH:MM' / '-HH:MM'."""
    z = t_local.strftime("%z")
    return f"{z[:3]}:{z[3:]}"


def hhmm(t_local: datetime, day: date | None = None) -> str:
    """Local wall-clock 'HH:MM'. With `day`, a time at midnight after that day is written '24:00'."""
    if day is not None and t_local.date() > day and t_local.hour == 0 and t_local.minute == 0:
        return "24:00"
    return t_local.strftime("%H:%M")

## Context

  the status back to `live` and starts with the next data drop.

  onboarding client without a config is reported as pending, not as an error.
- Deleting a client's files needs its own decision record.

steps.message:
Two things follow from that. Adding `configs/northwind.yaml` will flip the registry from "pending" to a real config, so the registry entry and the two tests that pin "pending" need updating as part of go-live. ADR 0007 also says new clients use config schema 2, so the Northwind config will use that.

My plan, with all new behaviour gated by config keys so the live clients keep their current outputs:

- **Ingest:** use the per-row `utc_offset` and snap stray minutes; build the full ISO-week grid (338 intervals for W44).
- **Staffing:** per-interval AHT (fixing a bug where interval mode averaged to a scalar), and apply the 0.85 occupancy cap when enabled.
- **Scheduler:** 11h rest, split shifts for PT only, break placement by surplus, and a repair loop so coverage holds net of breaks.
- **Evaluator:** SOW denominators, plus `required_hours`.

I'll start with the defaults and schema keys.

arguments.old_string:
min_cover: {}                 # per-queue floors, e.g. {chat: {agents: 2, hours: [20, 24]}} (wfm/constraints.py)
cross_skill_weight: 0.5       # an agent on another queue holding the floor queue's skill counts this much toward it

weekly_hours: {FT: 40, PT: 24}   # elapsed hours per ISO week
max_consecutive_days: 5
break:
  min_shift_hours: 6          # shifts at least this long get one break
  minutes: 20
  window_hours: [2, 5]        # break starts between these many hours after shift start
arguments.new_string:
min_cover: {}                 # per-queue floors, e.g. {chat: {agents: 2, hours: [20, 24]}} (wfm/constraints.py)
cross_skill_weight: 0.5       # an agent on another queue holding the floor queue's skill counts this much toward it

# Client-selectable rules. The values here keep the behaviour the live clients were scheduled with;
# a client file turns a rule on (Northwind: configs/northwind.yaml).
apply_occupancy_cap: false    # WFM-212: apply occupancy_cap in required staffing (open; not applied for existing clients)
sla_denominator: volume       # volume: attainment over intervals with volume; operating: every operating interval (SOW §1.4)
queue_operating_hours: {}     # per-queue local hours where the queue operates, e.g. {vip: [8, 20]}
min_rest_hours: 0             # elapsed hours between a shift's end and the agent's next start; 0 = no rule
split_contracts: null         # contracts allowed split shifts; null = any contract
net_of_breaks: false          # coverage must hold net of breaks (SOW §1.2); the scheduler adds agents where it does not

weekly_hours: {FT: 40, PT: 24}   # elapsed hours per ISO week
max_consecutive_days: 5
break:
  min_shift_hours: 6          # shifts at least this long get one break
  minutes: 20
  window_hours: [2, 5]        # break starts between these many hours after shift start
  placement: midpoint         # midpoint (shift midpoint) or surplus (SOW §2.3: largest gross coverage surplus in the window)

arguments.new_string:
def _read_export(path, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.read_csv(path, dtype={"utc_offset": str})
    local = pd.to_datetime(df["interval_start_local"])
    if "utc_offset" in df:
        # The offset on each row is authoritative (Northwind's README): it tells the repeated 01:00 hour
        # of a fall-back day apart. A stray minute (10:01 for 10:00) is snapped to the planning grain.
        local = local.dt.round(f"{cfg['interval_minutes']}min")
        labels = local.dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") + df["utc_offset"].str.replace(":", "", regex=False)
        df["interval_start_utc"] = pd.to_datetime(labels, format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M%z", utc=True)
        dup = df.duplicated(["queue", "interval_start_utc"], keep=False)
        if dup.any():
            raise SystemExit(f"{path.name}: {int(dup.sum())} rows share a queue and interval after snapping")
    elif cfg["client"] == "fabrikam":   # WFM-204
        df["interval_start_utc"] = _fixed_offsets(local, FABRIKAM_OFFSETS)
    else:
        df["interval_start_utc"] = local.dt.tz_localize(cfg["tz"]).dt.tz_convert("UTC")
    return df[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


def week_grid(week: str, tz: str, grain_min: int) -> pd.DatetimeIndex:
    """Every interval of the ISO week in the client's timezone, as UTC instants: local Monday 00:00 to
    the next local Monday 00:00 (169 hours in a week that ends DST, so 338 half-hours)."""
    z = ZoneInfo(tz)
    mon = iso_week_monday(week)
    start = datetime(mon.year, mon.month, mon.day, tzinfo=z)
    end = start + timedelta(days=7)   # wall-clock arithmetic, as in wfm.weeks.bounds_utc
    return pd.date_range(start.astimezone(timezone.utc), end.astimezone(timezone.utc),
                         freq=f"{grain_min}min", inclusive="left")

Two input layouts are supported in data/<client>/:

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, timedelta

import pandas as pd

from wfm.config import DATA_DIR

QUEUES = ("priority", "standard")


def iso_week_monday(week: str) -> date:
    """'2026-W44' -> Monday 2026-10-26."""
    year, wk = week.split("-W")
    return date.fromisocalendar(int(year), int(wk), 1)


def local_days(week: str, tz: str) -> list[date]:
    mon = iso_week_monday(week)
    return [mon + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(7)]


def _read_canonical(path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.read_csv(path)
    df["interval_start_utc"] = pd.to_datetime(df["interval_start_utc"], utc=True)
    return df[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


# Fabrikam's re-sent 2025 exports have no offset column. US Eastern offset in effect from each DST
# change date (local) on; good enough for Fabrikam's weeks (WFM-204).
FABRIKAM_OFFSETS = {"2025-03-09": "-04:00", "2025-11-02": "-05:00", "2026-03-08": "-04:00", "2026-11-01": "-05:00"}


def _fixed_offsets(local: pd.Series, table: dict[str, str]) -> pd.Series:
    """UTC from local wall-clock labels and a {change date: offset} table."""
    keys = sorted(table)
    off = [table[max([k for k in keys if k <= d] or keys[:1])] for d in local.dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")]
    return pd.to_datetime(local.dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") + pd.Series(off, index=local.index),
                          format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M%z", utc=True)


def _read_export(path, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.read_csv(path)
    local = pd.to_datetime(df["interval_start_local"])
    if cfg["client"] == "fabrikam" and "utc_offset" not in df:   # WFM-204
        df["interval_start_utc"] = _fixed_offsets(local, FABRIKAM_OFFSETS)
    else:
        df["interval_start_utc"] = local.dt.tz_localize(cfg["tz"]).dt.tz_convert("UTC")
    return df[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


def _resample(df: pd.DataFrame, grain_min: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Aggregate to the configured grain: volume summed, AHT volume-weighted."""
    df = df.copy()
    df["interval_start_utc"] = df["interval_start_utc"].dt.floor(f"{grain_min}min")
    df["_w"] = df["volume"] * df["aht_sec"]
    g = df.groupby(["queue", "interval_start_utc"], sort=True).agg(
        volume=("volume", "sum"), _w=("_w", "sum"), aht_mean=("aht_sec", "mean")).reset_index()
    g["aht_sec"] = (g["_w"] / g["volume"]).where(g["volume"] > 0, g["aht_mean"])
    return g[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


def load_week(cfg: dict, week: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    client = cfg["client"]
    grain = cfg["interval_minutes"]
    canon = DATA_DIR / client / f"week_{week}.csv"
    export = DATA_DIR / client / f"export_{week}.csv"
    if canon.exists():
        df = _read_canonical(canon)
    elif export.exists():
        df = _read_export(export, cfg)
    else:
        raise SystemExit(f"no data for {client} {week}: expected {canon} or {export}")

    df = _resample(df, grain)
    grid = pd.DatetimeIndex(sorted(df["interval_start_utc"].unique()))   # the week as the data delivers it
    frames = []
    for q in QUEUES:
        part = df[df["queue"] == q].set_index("interval_start_utc").reindex(grid)
        part["queue"] = q
        part["volume"] = part["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        part["aht_sec"] = part["aht_sec"].fillna(part["aht_sec"].mean())
        frames.append(part.rename_axis("interval_start_utc").reset_index())
    out = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    out["client"] = client
    out["interval_minutes"] = grain
    out = out.sort_values(["interval_start_utc", "queue"], kind="stable").reset_index(drop=True)

import pandas as pd

from vendor.qlib import required_agents as qlib_required
from wfm.staffing.erlang import required_agents


def _handle_time(g: pd.DataFrame, mode: str) -> pd.Series:
    """Handle time per interval under the configured smoothing (`aht_smoothing`):
    `queue_mean` (default) — the queue's mean AHT over intervals with volume; `interval` — each row's own AHT."""
    if mode == "interval":
        return g["aht_sec"]
    return pd.Series(g.loc[g["volume"] > 0, "aht_sec"].mean(), index=g.index)


def _model(cfg: dict):
    """Queueing model for required staffing (`queueing`): `erlang` — wfm/staffing/erlang.py, the

    template: Template
    day: date
    segments: list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]
    intervals: list[datetime] = field(default_factory=list)   # grid slots the segments cover
    break_start: datetime | None = None
    break_minutes: int = 0

    @property
    def hours(self) -> float:
        return sum((e - s).total_seconds() for s, e in self.segments) / 3600.0


def _covered(segments, day_grid) -> list[datetime]:
    return [t for s, e in segments for t in day_grid if s <= t < e]


MAX_REPAIR_ROUNDS = 60


def schedule_week(req: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent], week: str) -> list[Shift]:
    """Place the shifts, then the breaks. With `net_of_breaks`, an interval that a break leaves short
    of its requirement gets one more agent to cover it, and the week is placed again, until coverage
    holds net of breaks (SOW §1.2) or the rounds run out."""
    extra: dict[tuple[str, datetime], int] = defaultdict(int)
    for _ in range(MAX_REPAIR_ROUNDS):
        shifts = _place(req, cfg, agents, week, extra)
        place_breaks(shifts, cfg, req)
        if not cfg.get("net_of_breaks"):
            break
        short = net_shortfalls(shifts, req)
        if not short:
            break
        for key in short:
            extra[key] += 1
    return shifts


def net_shortfalls(shifts: list[Shift], req: pd.DataFrame) -> list[tuple[str, datetime]]:
    """(queue, interval) where agents on the queue, less those on break in the interval, fall short of the
    requirement."""
    gross: dict[tuple[str, datetime], int] = defaultdict(int)
    on_break: dict[tuple[str, datetime], int] = defaultdict(int)
    for sh in shifts:
        for t in sh.intervals:
            gross[(sh.queue, t)] += 1
        if sh.break_start is not None:
            on_break[(sh.queue, sh.break_start)] += 1
    short = []
    for q, g in req.groupby("queue"):
        for t, r in zip(g["interval_start_utc"], g["required"]):
            if r > gross[(q, t)] - on_break[(q, t)]:
                short.append((q, t))
    return short


def _place(req: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent], week: str, extra) -> list[Shift]:
    tz = cfg["tz"]
    grain_h = cfg["interval_minutes"] / 60.0
    caps = cfg["weekly_hours"]
    max_run = cfg["max_consecutive_days"]
    templates = templates_for(cfg)
    queues = list(dict.fromkeys(req["queue"]))
    min_rest = timedelta(hours=float(cfg.get("min_rest_hours") or 0))
    split_ok = cfg.get("split_contracts")       # contracts that may take a split shift; None = all

    # the requirement, raised where a break left the interval short (see schedule_week)
    required = {q: {t: r + extra.get((q, t), 0) for t, r in zip(g["interval_start_utc"], g["required"])}
                for q, g in req.groupby("queue")}
    cover = {q: defaultdict(int) for q in queues}
    cross = {q: defaultdict(int) for q in queues}    # agents on another queue holding this skill (min_cover)
    grid = sorted(set(req["interval_start_utc"]))
    z = ZoneInfo(tz)
    floors = {q: {t: constraints.floor(q, t, cfg) for t in grid} for q in queues}

    hours_used: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    days_worked: dict[str, list[date]] = defaultdict(list)
    last_end: dict[str, datetime] = {}          # end of each agent's latest shift (days go in order)
    shifts: list[Shift] = []

    for day in local_days(week, tz):
        day_grid = [t for t in grid if t.astimezone(z).date() == day]
        worked_today: set[str] = set()
        dead: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()   # (template, queue) pairs nobody can take today
        while True:
            best, best_val = None, 0.0
            for tpl in templates:
                segs = tpl.segments_utc(day, tz)
                ivs = _covered(segs, day_grid)
                for q in queues:
                    if (tpl.id, q) in dead:
                        continue
                    val = sum(min(1, constraints.uncovered(required[q][t], floors[q][t], cover[q][t], cross[q][t], cfg))
                              for t in ivs)
                    if val > best_val + 1e-9:
                        best, best_val = (tpl, q, segs, ivs), val
            if best is None or best_val * grain_h < 0.5:
                break
            tpl, q, segs, ivs = best
            start = segs[0][0]
            cands = [a for a in agents
                     if q in a.skills and eligible(tpl, a.contract) and a.agent_id not in worked_today
                     and (not tpl.is_split or split_ok is None or a.contract in split_ok)
                     and (a.agent_id not in last_end or start - last_end[a.agent_id] >= min_rest)
                     and hours_used[a.agent_id] + tpl.hours <= caps[a.contract] + 1e-9
                     and not _would_exceed_run(days_worked[a.agent_id], day, max_run)]
            if not cands:
                dead.add((tpl.id, q))
                continue
            a = min(cands, key=lambda x: (hours_used[x.agent_id], x.agent_id))
            shifts.append(Shift(a.agent_id, q, tpl, day, segs, ivs))
            hours_used[a.agent_id] += tpl.hours
            last_end[a.agent_id] = segs[-1][1]
            days_worked[a.agent_id].append(day)
            worked_today.add(a.agent_id)
            for t in ivs:
                cover[q][t] += 1
                for other in a.skills & set(queues) - {q}:
                    cross[other][t] += 1

    return shifts


def _would_exceed_run(worked: list[date], day: date, max_run: int) -> bool:
    """True if working `day` would make more than max_run consecutive local days."""
    run = 0
    d = day - timedelta(days=1)
    while d in worked:
        run += 1
        d -= timedelta(days=1)
    return run >= max_run


def place_breaks(shifts: list[Shift], cfg: dict) -> None:
    """One break per long shift, on the covered interval nearest the shift midpoint."""
    rule = cfg["break"]
    length = timedelta(minutes=rule["minutes"])
    for sh in shifts:
        if sh.hours < rule["min_shift_hours"]:
            continue
        fits = [t for t in sh.intervals if any(s <= t and t + length <= e for s, e in sh.segments)]
        if not fits:
            continue
        mid = sh.segments[0][0] + timedelta(hours=sh.hours / 2)
        sh.break_start = min(fits, key=lambda t: (abs((t - mid).total_seconds()), t))
        sh.break_minutes = rule["minutes"]


def to_frame(shifts: list[Shift]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """schedule.csv rows: one per segment; the break sits on the segment that contains it."""
    rows = []
    for sh in shifts:
        for i, (s, e) in enumerate(sh.segments):
            has_break = sh.break_start is not None and s <= sh.break_start < e
            rows.append({
                "agent_id": sh.agent_id, "queue": sh.queue,
                "segment_start_utc": s.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
                "segment_end_utc": e.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
                "template_id": sh.template.id, "segment_idx": i,
                "break_start_utc": sh.break_start.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") if has_break else "",
                "break_minutes": sh.break_minutes if has_break else 0,
            })
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["agent_id", "queue", "segment_start_utc", "segment_end_utc",
                                     "template_id", "segment_idx", "break_start_utc", "break_minutes"])
    return df.sort_values(["segment_start_utc", "agent_id", "segment_idx"], kind="stable").reset_index(drop=True)

"""Evaluate a schedule.csv against the required curve: attainment, hours, constraint audit.

A convenience for engineers. Contractual evaluation is performed independently against each
client's SOW.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pandas as pd

from wfm import constraints
from wfm.roster import Agent


def _parse(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = df.copy()
    for c in ("segment_start_utc", "segment_end_utc", "break_start_utc"):
        df[c] = pd.to_datetime(df[c], utc=True)
    df["break_minutes"] = df["break_minutes"].fillna(0).astype(int)
    return df


def coverage(sched: pd.DataFrame, grid, grain_min: int, skills: dict | None = None) -> tuple[dict, dict, dict]:
    """Per queue per interval: gross agents on queue, agents on break (overlapping the slot), and
    agents on shift on another queue who hold this queue's skill (`skills`: agent_id -> skills)."""
    gross = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    on_break = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    cross = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    step = timedelta(minutes=grain_min)
    skills = skills or {}
    for r in sched.itertuples(index=False):
        for t in grid:
            if r.segment_start_utc <= t < r.segment_end_utc:
                gross[r.queue][t] += 1
                for q in skills.get(r.agent_id, ()):
                    if q != r.queue:
                        cross[q][t] += 1
                if r.break_minutes and r.break_start_utc < t + step and t < r.break_start_utc + timedelta(minutes=int(r.break_minutes)):
                    on_break[r.queue][t] += 1
    return gross, on_break, cross


def evaluate(req: pd.DataFrame, sched: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent], week: str) -> dict:
    sched = _parse(sched)
    grain = cfg["interval_minutes"]
    grid = sorted(set(req["interval_start_utc"]))
    gross, on_break, cross = coverage(sched, grid, grain, {a.agent_id: a.skills for a in agents})
    h = grain / 60.0
    basis = cfg.get("attainment_basis", "service_level")

    sla, under, over = {}, 0.0, 0.0
    for q, g in req.groupby("queue"):
        met = tot = 0
        for r in g.itertuples(index=False):
            if r.volume <= 0:
                continue
            tot += 1
            scheduled = gross[q][r.interval_start_utc] - on_break[q][r.interval_start_utc]
            if basis == "coverage":   # PR #47: scheduled coverage of the requirement, capped at 1
                met += min(1.0, scheduled / r.required) if r.required else 1.0
            elif scheduled >= r.required:
                met += 1
            under += max(0, r.required - scheduled) * h
            over += max(0, scheduled - r.required) * h
        sla[q] = round(met / tot, 3) if tot else 1.0

    hours = float(((sched["segment_end_utc"] - sched["segment_start_utc"]).dt.total_seconds() / 3600).sum())
    return {
        "client": cfg["client"], "week": week, "intervals": len(grid),
        "sla": sla, "meets_target": all(v >= cfg["sla_target"] for v in sla.values()),
        "scheduled_hours": round(hours, 1),
        "understaffed_interval_hours": round(under, 1), "overstaffed_interval_hours": round(over, 1),
        "agents_scheduled": int(sched["agent_id"].nunique()),
        "violations": {**audit(sched, cfg, agents), "min_cover": floor_gaps(gross, cross, grid, cfg)},
    }


def floor_gaps(gross: dict, cross: dict, grid, cfg: dict) -> int:
    """Intervals where a `min_cover` queue has less cover than its floor (see wfm/constraints.py)."""
    return sum(1 for q in (cfg.get("min_cover") or {}) for t in grid
               if constraints.cover(gross[q][t], cross[q][t], cfg) < constraints.floor(q, t, cfg))


def audit(sched: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent]) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Count violations of the service's standard rules per agent."""
    by_id = {a.agent_id: a for a in agents}
    z = ZoneInfo(cfg["tz"])
    v = {"weekly_hours": 0, "consecutive_days": 0, "skill_match": 0, "no_overlap": 0}
    for aid, g in sched.groupby("agent_id"):
        a = by_id.get(aid)
        g = g.sort_values("segment_start_utc")
        hours = ((g["segment_end_utc"] - g["segment_start_utc"]).dt.total_seconds() / 3600).sum()
        if a is None or hours > cfg["weekly_hours"][a.contract] + 1e-9:
            v["weekly_hours"] += 1
        if a is not None and any(q not in a.skills for q in g["queue"]):
            v["skill_match"] += 1
        ends = g["segment_end_utc"].shift(1)
        if (g["segment_start_utc"] < ends).any():
            v["no_overlap"] += 1
        days = sorted({t.astimezone(z).date() for t in g["segment_start_utc"]})
        run = 1
        for d1, d2 in zip(days, days[1:]):
            run = run + 1 if (d2 - d1).days == 1 else 1
            if run > cfg["max_consecutive_days"]:
                v["consecutive_days"] += 1
                break
    return v

The diagnosis is clear:

- **Priority and standard are heavily overstaffed**: 1170 and 1320 net agent-intervals against 762 and 857 required. The greedy overcovers, and the surplus should be removable.
- **VIP is capacity-limited.** All 11 VIP-skilled FT agents are used at 40h (440h total). The floor forces three shifts a day, which uses about 168h, leaving too little for the VIP requirement.

The first fix is a trim pass for the surplus. It removes any shift whose removal keeps the week feasible: net-of-break coverage, floors, and break placement all re-checked. It's gated by `trim_surplus` so the live clients are untouched.

"""Greedy template placement, one local day at a time.

For each local day of the week: while some (template, queue) pair still covers at least half an
hour of uncovered requirement, place the best-scoring pair on the available agent with the fewest
hours so far. Breaks go at the shift midpoint. Deterministic: fixed template order, agent ids as
the tie-break.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pandas as pd

from wfm import constraints
from wfm.ingest.loader import local_days
from wfm.roster import Agent
from wfm.scheduler.templates import Template, eligible, templates_for


@dataclass
class Shift:
    agent_id: str
    queue: str
    template: Template
    day: date
    segments: list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]
    intervals: list[datetime] = field(default_factory=list)   # grid slots the segments cover
    break_start: datetime | None = None
    break_minutes: int = 0

    @property
    def hours(self) -> float:
        return sum((e - s).total_seconds() for s, e in self.segments) / 3600.0


def _covered(segments, day_grid) -> list[datetime]:
    return [t for s, e in segments for t in day_grid if s <= t < e]


MAX_REPAIR_ROUNDS = 60


def schedule_week(req: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent], week: str) -> list[Shift]:
    """Place the shifts, then the breaks. With `net_of_breaks`, an interval that a break leaves short
    of its requirement gets one more agent to cover it, and the week is placed again, until coverage
    holds net of breaks (SOW §1.2) or the rounds run out."""
    extra: dict[tuple[str, datetime], int] = defaultdict(int)
    for _ in range(MAX_REPAIR_ROUNDS):
        shifts = _place(req, cfg, agents, week, extra)
        place_breaks(shifts, cfg, req)
        if not cfg.get("net_of_breaks"):
            break
        short = net_shortfalls(shifts, req)
        if not short:
            break
        for key in short:
            extra[key] += 1
    return shifts


def net_shortfalls(shifts: list[Shift], req: pd.DataFrame) -> list[tuple[str, datetime]]:
    """(queue, interval) where agents on the queue, less those on break in the interval, fall short of the
    requirement."""
    gross: dict[tuple[str, datetime], int] = defaultdict(int)
    on_break: dict[tuple[str, datetime], int] = defaultdict(int)
    for sh in shifts:
        for t in sh.intervals:
            gross[(sh.queue, t)] += 1
        if sh.break_start is not None:
            on_break[(sh.queue, sh.break_start)] += 1
    short = []
    for q, g in req.groupby("queue"):
        for t, r in zip(g["interval_start_utc"], g["required"]):
            if r > gross[(q, t)] - on_break[(q, t)]:
                short.append((q, t))
    return short


def _place(req: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent], week: str, extra) -> list[Shift]:
    tz = cfg["tz"]
    grain_h = cfg["interval_minutes"] / 60.0
    caps = cfg["weekly_hours"]
    max_run = cfg["max_consecutive_days"]
    templates = templates_for(cfg)
    queues = list(dict.fromkeys(req["queue"]))
    min_rest = timedelta(hours=float(cfg.get("min_rest_hours") or 0))
    split_ok = cfg.get("split_contracts")       # contracts that may take a split shift; None = all

    # the requirement, raised where a break left the interval short (see schedule_week)
    required = {q: {t: r + extra.get((q, t), 0) for t, r in zip(g["interval_start_utc"], g["required"])}
                for q, g in req.groupby("queue")}
    cover = {q: defaultdict(int) for q in queues}
    cross = {q: defaultdict(int) for q in queues}    # agents on another queue holding this skill (min_cover)
    grid = sorted(set(req["interval_start_utc"]))
    z = ZoneInfo(tz)
    floors = {q: {t: constraints.floor(q, t, cfg) for t in grid} for q in queues}

    hours_used: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    days_worked: dict[str, list[date]] = defaultdict(list)
    last_end: dict[str, datetime] = {}          # end of each agent's latest shift (days go in order)
    shifts: list[Shift] = []

    for day in local_days(week, tz):
        day_grid = [t for t in grid if t.astimezone(z).date() == day]
        worked_today: set[str] = set()
        dead: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()   # (template, queue) pairs nobody can take today
        while True:
            best, best_val = None, 0.0
            for tpl in templates:
                segs = tpl.segments_utc(day, tz)
                ivs = _covered(segs, day_grid)
                for q in queues:
                    if (tpl.id, q) in dead:
                        continue
                    val = sum(min(1, constraints.uncovered(required[q][t], floors[q][t], cover[q][t], cross[q][t], cfg))
                              for t in ivs)
                    if val > best_val + 1e-9:
                        best, best_val = (tpl, q, segs, ivs), val
            if best is None or best_val * grain_h < 0.5:
                break
            tpl, q, segs, ivs = best
            start = segs[0][0]
            cands = [a for a in agents

    """True if working `day` would make more than max_run consecutive local days."""
    run = 0

    while d in worked:
        run += 1
        d -= timedelta(days=1)
    return run >= max_run

    gross coverage surplus (agents on the queue, ignoring breaks, less the requirement) is largest; a tie

    length = timedelta(minutes=rule["minutes"])
    surplus_mode = rule.get("placement", "midpoint") == "surplus"
    if surplus_mode:

        gross: dict[tuple[str, datetime], int] = defaultdict(int)
        for sh in shifts:

        required = {(q, t): r for q, g in req.groupby("queue")

steps.message:
The bound settles the VIP question. Covering every VIP interval at its requirement needs about 534 hours and 73 shifts a week, against 440 hours and 55 shifts available. So 0.95 is not reachable for VIP with this roster. That makes VIP a §2.7 exception, and the exception should report the best VIP attainment I can actually schedule.

The shortfall is not the whole problem, though. The 56 uncovered VIP floor intervals violate §2.6, which is a hard rule. The greedy starves the floor because it spends the VIP hours on daytime demand first. The fix is a floor-first plan for VIP: a per-day enumeration of template mixes that holds the floor, a week-long DP on hours, then assignment under the same rest and run rules. Other queues are placed afterwards with the VIP shifts as prior state. I'll re-read greedy.py and rewrite it as one coherent file.

46	def schedule_week(req: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent], week: str) -> list[Shift]:
47	    """Place the shifts, then the breaks. With `net_of_breaks`, an interval that a break leaves short
48	    of its requirement gets one more agent to cover it, and the week is placed again, until coverage
49	    holds net of breaks (SOW §1.2) or the rounds run out."""
50	    extra: dict[tuple[str, datetime], int] = defaultdict(int)
51	    for _ in range(MAX_REPAIR_ROUNDS):
52	        shifts = _place(req, cfg, agents, week, extra)
53	        place_breaks(shifts, cfg, req)
54	        short = net_shortfalls(shifts, req) if cfg.get("net_of_breaks") else []
55	        if not short:
56	            break
57	        for key in short:
58	            extra[key] += 1
59	    if cfg.get("trim_surplus") and cfg.get("net_of_breaks"):
60	        shifts = trim_surplus(shifts, req, cfg, agents)
61	    return shifts

64	def _tally(shifts: list[Shift], skills: dict[str, frozenset]):
65	    """Gross agents per (queue, interval), and the agents on another queue who hold that queue's skill."""
66	    gross: dict[tuple[str, datetime], int] = defaultdict(int)
67	    cross: dict[tuple[str, datetime], int] = defaultdict(int)
68	    for sh in shifts:
69	        for t in sh.intervals:
70	            gross[(sh.queue, t)] += 1
71	            for skill in skills.get(sh.agent_id, ()):
72	                if skill != sh.queue:
73	                    cross[(skill, t)] += 1
74	    return gross, cross

77	def _feasible(shifts: list[Shift], req: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, skills: dict[str, frozenset]) -> bool:
78	    place_breaks(shifts, cfg, req)
79	    if net_shortfalls(shifts, req):
80	        return False
81	    gross, cross = _tally(shifts, skills)
82	    for q, t in zip(req["queue"], req["interval_start_utc"]):
83	        floor = constraints.floor(q, t, cfg)
84	        if floor and constraints.cover(gross[(q, t)], cross[(q, t)], cfg) < floor:
85	            return False
86	    return True

89	def trim_surplus(shifts: list[Shift], req: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent]) -> list[Shift]:
90	    """Drop shifts, most-surplus first, while the week stays feasible: coverage holds net of breaks, the
91	    floors hold and breaks sit where the rule puts them. Removing a shift never adds a rule violation,
92	    so only the coverage and the efficiency bound (SOW §1.6) change."""
93	    skills = {a.agent_id: a.skills for a in agents}
94	    required = {(q, t): r for q, t, r in zip(req["queue"], req["interval_start_utc"], req["required"])}
95	    keep = list(shifts)
96	    changed = True
97	    while changed:
98	        changed = False
99	        gross, _ = _tally(keep, skills)
100	        surplus = {id(sh): sum(gross[(sh.queue, t)] - required.get((sh.queue, t), 0) for t in sh.intervals)
101	                   for sh in keep}
102	        for sh in sorted(keep, key=lambda s: -surplus[id(s)]):
103	            cand = [s for s in keep if s is not sh]
104	            if _feasible(cand, req, cfg, skills):
105	                keep = cand
106	                changed = True
107	    place_breaks(keep, cfg, req)
108	    return keep

111	def net_shortfalls(shifts: list[Shift], req: pd.DataFrame) -> list[tuple[str, datetime]]:
112	    """(queue, interval) where agents on the queue, less those on break in the interval, fall short of the
113	    requirement."""
114	    gross: dict[tuple[str, datetime], int] = defaultdict(int)
115	    on_break: dict[tuple[str, datetime], int] = defaultdict(int)
116	    for sh in shifts:
117	        for t in sh.intervals:
118	            gross[(sh.queue, t)] += 1
119	        if sh.break_start is not None:
120	            on_break[(sh.queue, sh.break_start)] += 1
121	    short = []
122	    for q, g in req.groupby("queue"):
123	        for t, r in zip(g["interval_start_utc"], g["required"]):
124	            if r > gross[(q, t)] - on_break[(q, t)]:
125	                short.append((q, t))
126	    return short

129	def _place(req: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent], week: str, extra) -> list[Shift]:
130	    tz = cfg["tz"]
131	    grain_h = cfg["interval_minutes"] / 60.0
132	    caps = cfg["weekly_hours"]
133	    max_run = cfg["max_consecutive_days"]
134	    templates = templates_for(cfg)
135	    queues = list(dict.fromkeys(req["queue"]))
136	    min_rest = timedelta(hours=float(cfg.get("min_rest_hours") or 0))
137	    split_ok = cfg.get("split_contracts")       # contracts that may take a split shift; None = all
138	    weight = {q: float((cfg.get("queue_weight") or {}).get(q, 1.0)) for q in queues}   # placement priority
139	
140	    # the requirement, raised where a break left the interval short (see schedule_week)
141	    required = {q: {t: r + extra.get((q, t), 0) for t, r in zip(g["interval_start_utc"], g["required"])}

144	    cross = {q: defaultdict(int) for q in queues}    # agents on another queue holding this skill (min_cover)

147	    floors = {q: {t: constraints.floor(q, t, cfg) for t in grid} for q in queues}
148	
149	    hours_used: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
150	    days_worked: dict[str, list[date]] = defaultdict(list)
151	    last_end: dict[str, datetime] = {}          # end of each agent's latest shift (days go in order)
152	    shifts: list[Shift] = []
153	
154	    for day in local_days(week, tz):
155	        day_grid = [t for t in grid if t.astimezone(z).date() == day]
156	        worked_today: set[str] = set()
157	        dead: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()   # (template, queue) pairs nobody can take today
158	        while True:
159	            best, best_val = None, 0.0
160	            for tpl in templates:
161	                segs = tpl.segments_utc(day, tz)
162	                ivs = _covered(segs, day_grid)
163	                for q in queues:
164	                    if (tpl.id, q) in dead:
165	                        continue
166	                    val = weight[q] * sum(min(1, constraints.uncovered(required[q][t], floors[q][t], cover[q][t], cross[q][t], cfg))
167	                              for t in ivs)

170	            if best is None or best_val * grain_h < 0.5:

172	            tpl, q, segs, ivs = best
173	            start = segs[0][0]
174	            cands = [a for a in agents
175	                     if q in a.skills and eligible(tpl, a.contract) and a.agent_id not in worked_today
176	                     and (not tpl.is_split or split_ok is None or a.contract in split_ok)
177	                     and (a.agent_id not in last_end or start - last_end[a.agent_id] >= min_rest)

179	                     and not _would_exceed_run(days_worked[a.agent_id], day, max_run)]
180	            if not cands:
181	                dead.add((tpl.id, q))
182	                continue
183	            a = min(cands, key=lambda x: (hours_used[x.agent_id], x.agent_id))
184	            shifts.append(Shift(a.agent_id, q, tpl, day, segs, ivs))
185	            hours_used[a.agent_id] += tpl.hours
186	            last_end[a.agent_id] = segs[-1][1]
187	            days_worked[a.agent_id].append(day)
188	            worked_today.add(a.agent_id)
189	            for t in ivs:
190	                cover[q][t] += 1
191	                for other in a.skills & set(queues) - {q}:

197	def _would_exceed_run(worked: list[date], day: date, max_run: int) -> bool:
198	    """True if working `day` would make more than max_run consecutive local days."""
199	    run = 0
200	    d = day - timedelta(days=1)
201	    while d in worked:
202	        run += 1
203	        d -= timedelta(days=1)
204	    return run >= max_run

207	def place_breaks(shifts: list[Shift], cfg: dict, req: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
208	    """One break per long shift. `midpoint`: on the covered interval nearest the shift midpoint.
209	    `surplus` (SOW §2.3): in the window of hours after the shift start, on the planning interval whose
210	    gross coverage surplus (agents on the queue, ignoring breaks, less the requirement) is largest; a tie
211	    goes to the earlier interval."""
212	    rule = cfg["break"]
213	    length = timedelta(minutes=rule["minutes"])
214	    surplus_mode = rule.get("placement", "midpoint") == "surplus"
215	    if surplus_mode:
216	        lo, hi = rule["window_hours"]
217	        gross: dict[tuple[str, datetime], int] = defaultdict(int)
218	        for sh in shifts:
219	            for t in sh.intervals:
220	                gross[(sh.queue, t)] += 1
221	        required = {(q, t): r for q, g in req.groupby("queue")
222	                    for t, r in zip(g["interval_start_utc"], g["required"])}
223	    for sh in shifts:
224	        sh.break_start, sh.break_minutes = None, 0
225	        if sh.hours < rule["min_shift_hours"]:
226	            continue
227	        if surplus_mode:
228	            start = sh.segments[0][0]
229	            window = [t for t in sh.intervals
230	                      if lo <= (t - start).total_seconds() / 3600 <= hi
231	                      and any(s <= t and t + length <= e for s, e in sh.segments)]
232	            if window:
233	                sh.break_start = min(window, key=lambda t: (-(gross[(sh.queue, t)] - required.get((sh.queue, t), 0)), t))

235	            continue
236	        fits = [t for t in sh.intervals if any(s <= t and t + length <= e for s, e in sh.segments)]
237	        if not fits:
238	            continue
239	        mid = sh.segments[0][0] + timedelta(hours=sh.hours / 2)
240	        sh.break_start = min(fits, key=lambda t: (abs((t - mid).total_seconds()), t))
241	        sh.break_minutes = rule["minutes"]

244	def to_frame(shifts: list[Shift]) -> pd.DataFrame:
245	    """schedule.csv rows: one per segment; the break sits on the segment that contains it."""
246	    rows = []
247	    for sh in shifts:
248	        for i, (s, e) in enumerate(sh.segments):
249	            has_break = sh.break_start is not None and s <= sh.break_start < e
250	            rows.append({

252	                "segment_start_utc": s.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
253	                "segment_end_utc": e.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
254	                "template_id": sh.template.id, "segment_idx": i,
255	                "break_start_utc": sh.break_start.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") if has_break else "",
256	                "break_minutes": sh.break_minutes if has_break else 0,

258	    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["agent_id", "queue", "segment_start_utc", "segment_end_utc",
259	                                     "template_id", "segment_idx", "break_start_utc", "break_minutes"])
260	    return df.sort_values(["segment_start_utc", "agent_id", "segment_idx"], kind="stable").reset_index(drop=True)
